title: Choose the look for your Start Where You Are page
question: The roll dealt Measuring Cups. Keep it, take my pick or the alternate, or re-roll for a new hand (safer or bolder).

options.label: Measuring Cups
options.lineage: Glass kitchen measuring jugs with red printed graduations, and the idea of filling your cup
options.thesis: Health, Work, Play and Love as four glass measuring cups, each filled to your score.
materials: clear glass with red printed graduation marks
four different drinks: green juice, coffee, orange soda, berry
a strip of masking tape with a handwritten label
options.viewport: Four tall cups in a row on a cool white counter. Each liquid sits at its % with the red tick marks beside it. Under each cup is its area name, a large score, and your note in a calm column. On a phone the cups become one horizontal shelf you can swipe.
options.risk: It could feel kitschy if the cups are drawn cutesy instead of precise like real lab glass; the kitchen idea also has nothing to do with the book itself.

raised.raise: The lowest cup carries a physical mark, a folded tape flag reading 'start here', so the biggest gap is a mark rather than just a color.
All four cups share one 0–100 ruler in steps of 10 as their only scale, so they compare honestly side by side.
Each fill level also gets a written label, like 'a splash', 'half full', or 'brimming', so the reading never depends on color alone.
Every cup has the same label layout (area, score, note), like a printed end label.

options.label: Paint Chip Cards
options.lineage: Hardware-store paint swatch strips, light to deep in one hue
options.thesis: Each area is a paint strip of ten chips, colored in up to your score and named like a paint color.
materials: a punched hole at the top
options.viewport: Four tall swatch strips fanned slightly. Each has ten chips, colored in up to the score with the rest left blank. A paint-style name for the level and your note sit on the strip's white base.
options.risk: This is my top pick, and paint-swatch styling is a familiar 'fun' move; it lands well, but it's less surprising.
options.case: Four hues for four areas, and a light-to-deep ladder is a natural 0–100 gauge.

options.label: Pop Record Sleeve
options.thesis: Your check-in as a four-track EP, with each area a track on a flat, saturated sleeve.
options.viewport: A flat tangerine field with a rounded logotype 'Start Where You Are', and four track lines tucked into a corner, sorted by score. Choosing a track cross-fades the background to that area's color and shows its note.
options.case: Four tracks is a closed set of four, which fits the four areas well. It's very fun, but the score is just a number, so the gauge is weaker.
options.risk: Notes are revealed one at a time, so you can't take in all four at a glance.

options.label: Theater Cyclorama Dawn
options.lineage: Stage lighting moving from night to day
options.thesis: Each score as a phase of dawn.
options.viewport: Horizon bands from dark to light.
options.kept: Written level labels so color is never the only signal.

options.label: Sneaker Box Wall
options.lineage: Stacked shoe boxes with end labels
options.thesis: Four boxes; lift the lid to read a note.
options.viewport: A stack of boxes showing their end labels.
options.case: Hiding the notes hurts reading at a glance.
options.kept: One shared label layout for every area.

options.label: Darkroom Exposure Record
options.kept: One shared tonal ruler as the only scale.

options.label: Film Cutting Bench
options.thesis: Areas as frames along a rail.
options.viewport: A perforated strip across the page.
options.risk: Built for a workflow you don't have.
options.case: It's a tool, not a reflection.
options.kept: State shown as a mark: a 'start here' flag on the lowest area.

canonCard.label: Standard dashboard
canonCard.thesis: A clean wellness dashboard: four cards with ring gauges, done well.
canonCard.viewport: A header, then a 2×2 grid of cards, each with a ring gauge, a %, and a note.
canonCard.risk: It looks like every app dashboard; it's clean, but probably not 'fun'.
